docs.title: agentkit
docs.text:
agentkit is a model-neutral Python framework for building agent harnesses. It has one model execution path: CallRuntime. AgentRunner composes agent instructions, context, tools, skills, delegation, and verification on top of that runtime.

The host application owns workflow orchestration, durable business state, and domain-specific grading. agentkit supplies the model call, tool loop, events, continuation, accounting, and hooks that a host can compose into its harness.

docs.title: The runtime and the harness
docs.text:
Use CallRuntime.ask() for a single request or CallRuntime.run() for a bounded tool loop. Use AgentRunner.run_agent() when you want agent definitions, minds, prompt composition, scoped tools, and memory providers. Both call the same runtime and return the same Answer and Usage contracts.

import asyncio

from agentkit.agents import AgentDefinition, AgentRunner, InstructionSet
from agentkit.core.runtime import CallRuntime
from agentkit.models.contracts import ModelMode


async def main() -> None:
    # Supply an adapter configured for the selected mode/model.
    adapter = ...
    async with CallRuntime() as runtime:
        runner = AgentRunner(runtime)
        answer = await runner.run_agent(
            AgentDefinition(
                name="assistant",
                mode=ModelMode.OPENAI_API,
                model="your-configured-model",
                instructions=InstructionSet(system="Answer clearly and accurately."),
            ),
            "What does this service do?",
            adapter=adapter,
        )
        print(answer.text)


asyncio.run(main())

The package supports Anthropic API, OpenAI API, Claude Code CLI, and Codex CLI adapters. Runtime behavior belongs in the shared runtime; adapters translate provider requests and responses. Provider-specific capability limits are surfaced explicitly.

docs.title: What plugs into the harness
docs.text:
• Minds define reasoning strategy independently of model transport.
  • Tools are declared with side-effect metadata, validated, scoped, and dispatched by the current runtime path.
  • Context travels with messages and can be transformed by a context policy between slices or before resume.
  • Memory providers contribute untrusted context during prompt composition.
  • Skills provide approved resources and can emit lifecycle events.
  • EventHub exposes call and agent events to host subscribers. Subscribers can opt into isolated failure handling.
  • Pricing, limits, output validation, retries, and continuation are configured through the runtime call contract.

See the build plan for the implementation source of truth and the Mirror gap record for the history and evidence behind those requirements. The runnable examples live under tests/examples; offline tests live under tests/source, and provider-backed evaluations live under tests/evals.

docs.title: Publishing agentkit
docs.text: How releases work. Read this before your first release.

docs.title: PyPI distribution name
docs.text:
Distribution name: arc-agentkit (the string you pip install). Import name: agentkit (unchanged — every existing user of from agentkit import ... keeps working).

PyPI's namespace for agentkit is owned by a different unrelated project (vik@japanvik.net, "distributed llm agent swarms", v0.0.4 · Mar 2026). Reserving a brand-attributed name keeps discovery clean and preserves the import agentkit ergonomics.

The distinction is standard in Python packaging — e.g. pip install Django → import django, pip install python-dotenv → import dotenv.

docs.title: Release flow (once per version)
docs.text: We publish via PyPI Trusted Publisher (OIDC) — no long-lived PyPI API tokens live in the repo or in secrets. GitHub Actions signs a request to PyPI, PyPI verifies against the trusted-publisher configuration on the project page, and the release is uploaded. If you leaked a token, PyPI would issue a warning and revoke; with OIDC there's no token to leak.

docs.title: One-time setup
docs.text:
1. Register the distribution on TestPyPI first (dry-run environment):
  2. Go to https://test.pypi.org/manage/account/publishing/
  3. "Add a new publisher"
  4. Owner: arc-labs-ai
  5. Repository: agentkit
  6. Workflow name: release.yml

  7. Environment: pypi (matches the environment: block in release.yml)

  8. Same again for real PyPI:

  9. https://pypi.org/manage/account/publishing/

  10. Same shape.

  11. First-time publish will fail on PyPI until PyPI has a version of the package registered. Options: register the name via an initial dummy release from the maintainer's account (bootstrap), OR publish to TestPyPI first and then request PyPI reserve the name.

docs.title: Every release
docs.text:
1. Update CHANGELOG.md — new entry at the top under the new version number (semver). Format: ## [0.2.0] - 2026-XX-XX + bullet list of changes.
  2. Bump version in pyproject.toml. Semver: patch for bug fix, minor for backward-compatible feature, major for breaking change.
  3. Merge to main with the changelog + version bump.
  4. Tag the commit with v<version> (matching pyproject exactly):
git tag v0.2.0 && git push origin v0.2.0
  1. GitHub Actions release.yml fires on the tag:
  2. Builds wheel + sdist via hatchling.
  3. Runs twine check dist/* to catch metadata errors before upload.
  4. Requests OIDC token, publishes to PyPI.

  5. Creates a GitHub Release with generated notes.

  6. Verify on PyPI (~2 minutes after publish):

pip install --upgrade arc-agentkit
python -c "from importlib.metadata import version; print(version('arc-agentkit'))"

docs.title: Local dry-run before tagging
docs.text:
Always run this before creating the tag:

make build          # hatchling → dist/*.whl + dist/*.tar.gz
make publish-dry    # twine check dist/*

If publish-dry complains about long-description rendering, README markdown, or invalid classifiers — fix those in the same commit as the changelog and version bump. Failing publishes leave dead space on the version list.

docs.title: SemVer policy
docs.text:
We're pre-1.0 (currently 0.x). Rules we hold:

  • Patch (0.x.PATCH) — bug fixes, docs, internal refactors that don't change the public API's behavior.
  • Minor (0.MINOR.0) — new public API surface OR intentional behavior changes to existing API surface. Log in CHANGELOG under "Changed" / "Deprecated" / "Removed" sections.
  • Major (MAJOR.0.0) — reserved for the 1.0 stabilization pass and any subsequent hard-breaking rewrites.

Public API = anything exported from agentkit/__init__.py or a top-level subpackage's __init__.py. Anything under _private.py or prefixed with _ is fair game to change in a patch release.

docs.title: Yanking a bad release
docs.text:
If a release ships broken:

pip install --upgrade twine
twine yank arc-agentkit 0.2.0 --reason "critical bug in X — use 0.2.1"

Yanking hides the version from pip install arc-agentkit (unbounded) but leaves pip install arc-agentkit==0.2.0 working for anyone who pinned it. Then ship the fixed version.

Never delete a released version. PyPI enforces this — deletions break downstream lockfiles for anyone who pinned to the yanked version.

docs.title: Common gotchas
docs.text:
• Trusted publisher misconfigured → 403 on upload. Check that the workflow file name in the publisher config matches release.yml exactly.
  • Wheel builds but sdist doesn't → hatchling's [tool.hatch.build] didn't include a source file. Add it to packages or include.
  • twine check warns about README → PyPI parses the README as reStructuredText by default. We set readme = "README.md" and PyPI handles the text/markdown content-type via content_type inference from the file extension. Make sure the content_type metadata field is set to text/markdown in the built wheel's METADATA.
  • Version mismatch between tag and pyproject.toml → CI fails early. Fix the mismatch before re-tagging.

docs.title: agentkit build plan
docs.text:
The ordered list of changes that makes agentkit the single, model-neutral agent runtime Mirror (and anyone else) builds on. It is the plan to work from. mirror-gaps.md is the record of how each item was found and measured; the item ids (G1–G53) are shared between the two.

Written 2026-10-13, against 5ebe4c0 plus the uncommitted working tree. Re-check each item's status against the code before starting it: some are partly done in the working tree.

docs.title: 0. Rules for every change
docs.text:
1. One runtime. CallRuntime (ask/run) and AgentRunner.run_agent on top of it are the only way to call a model. Nothing new may be built on the Invoker, its middleware, RunContext.services, Agent, Workflow or the other older modules. They are being deleted (Phase 3).
  2. Same behaviour on all four modes. Claude Code CLI, Codex CLI, Anthropic API and OpenAI API. Every behaviour lives in the runtime core, never in one adapter. An adapter only translates. Every behaviour gets a conformance scenario in tests/source/conformance/, run against each mode's fake, or explicitly marked not applicable to a mode with the reason.
  3. Test first, and prove the test can fail. Write the test, watch it fail for the stated reason, then implement. Every test has a clean twin, and a test that would pass with the code removed is not a test.
  4. Fakes must be as strict as the real thing. A fake CLI that accepts what the real CLI rejects hid G26. Every fake validates its inputs the way its real counterpart does.
  5. No backward-compatibility shims. Delete old paths in the same change that replaces them. Consumers on an older revision stay pinned until they move.
  6. No timers that mean ownership. No leases, heartbeats or renewals. Admission is the untimed acquire hook. A stall bound is the absence of events, never a wall clock on work that is still producing.
  7. Secrets never reach events, logs or snapshots. Masking is on by default, and the host can supply its own masker.
  8. Report results with their scope. "The conformance suite passes" and "the suite passes" are different claims.

docs.title: Phase 3: One runtime (G43)
docs.text:
Goal: one result type, one usage type, one path. Every feature that exists is reachable.

Do it in this order, so nothing breaks midway.

  1. Move the CLI adapter off the older runtime. The current CLI adapter still uses Agent, RunContext and Budget internally (models/providers/cli/calls.py:107,126,242-246,488-491). Replace them with what it actually needs.
  2. Done when: cli/calls.py imports nothing from the older modules, and all CLI conformance passes.
  3. Rebuild the pieces that have users, as hooks on the current path.
  4. Compaction: context_policy: Callable[[WorkingContext], WorkingContext], applied by run/run_agent between slices and before resume. It is per mode (G46): on the CLI it keeps --resume and sends nothing extra, rather than dropping the native session. Deterministic policies are built in; summarising policies are an explicit opt-in.
  5. Memory: a provider run_agent turns into an untrusted context part at compose time.
  6. Approvals: rebuild ApprovalServer on the current CLI adapter's --permission-prompt-tool, with the same callback shape as McpPolicy.approval.
  7. Done when:
    • the same transcript compacts to the same result twice;
    • a Claude fake keeps one resume id across three compacted slices;
    • memory items reach the prompt as an untrusted part;
    • a CLI permission prompt reaches the host callback.
  8. Delete the older runtime in one change:
  9. the Invoker, core/policies middleware and RunContext.services;
  10. Observation/ObserverPort and integrations/observers;
  11. state/checkpoints, replay, stores, vectors and leases;
  12. agents/workflows, agents/cognition, agents/policies, agents/control and agents/evaluation;
  13. Agent, RequestBuilder, skills.Skill.as_agent and tools/adapters.as_tool.

Keep core/guardrails as a library tools call, with an optional ToolSet hook. Update the docs and examples in the same change. 4. Architecture claims test: - one public Answer type and one Usage type; - a planted import of each deleted module is caught; - every public module is reachable from CallRuntime/AgentRunner, or declared a library.

docs.title: Order, and what each phase unlocks for Mirror
docs.text:
Phase Unlocks 1 Mirror's one-shot calls (cognition.ask) on API keys, with honest money 2 Mirror's agent loops (cognition.run_agent) for conversation and analysis 3 one runtime; Mirror's compaction and memory plug in as hooks instead of living in Mirror 4 Mirror's build service (forge) on agentkit: long, parallel, fenced, cached CLI sessions 5 running on real subscription logins in production

Phases 1 and 2 can run in parallel. Phase 3 step 1 must land before step 3. Phase 4 needs Phase 3's compaction hook (for G46 and G47). Phase 5 runs at the end of each phase on whatever it unlocked.

docs.title: Implementation status
docs.text: build-plan.md is the implementation source of truth. This page summarizes the current execution architecture and verification boundaries; it does not maintain a second item-by-item gap tracker. Historical evidence for consumer-derived requirements remains in mirror-gaps.md.

docs.title: Current architecture
docs.text:
• CallRuntime.ask() and CallRuntime.run() own model dispatch, continuation, retries, limits, pricing, structured output, tool execution, and call events.
  • AgentRunner.run_agent() composes agent instructions, minds, context, scoped tools, skills, memory, delegation, and verification on that runtime.
  • Anthropic API, OpenAI API, Claude Code CLI, and Codex CLI adapters translate the shared contracts. Provider capability limits remain explicit.
  • WorkingContext carries message context across model changes. Context policies transform that context at runtime boundaries. Memory providers contribute untrusted prompt context.
  • EventHub is the host-facing event subscription point. Isolated subscribers cannot fail publication; runtime event sinks report degradation while preserving the answer.
  • Hosts own business workflows, durable domain state, scheduling, and domain-specific grading.

docs.title: Verification scope
docs.text:
The offline source suite verifies runtime contracts against scripted API adapters and fake CLIs. The conformance suite must be reported separately from unit/source coverage. Architecture claims are checked by tests/source/architecture/test_single_runtime.py; that test does not substitute for behavior tests.

The latest full offline run passed 1,326 tests with 1 skipped. The conformance suite passed 407 tests, and the single-runtime architecture claims test passed 4 tests. uv run ruff check agentkit tests, git diff --check, and the strict MkDocs build pass after replacing the legacy-runtime documentation.

Historical provider-backed evaluations are retained under tests/evals/reports/. They use their recorded source digests and configured model/CLI versions; they do not establish a live matrix for the current working tree. The current revision has not yet run the four-mode live matrix or the real-login refresh checks. In particular, the macOS Claude Code keychain-versus-file behavior and a forced credential refresh remain unproven here. The current working-tree changes are not yet committed.

docs.title: Known provider limits
docs.text: Codex CLI does not expose mid-call cost enforcement or turn slicing; the runtime refuses a requested hard cost cap or turn slice before dispatch. Measured post-turn cost remains available when no hard cap is requested. Provider-native transport for very large structured schemas and native Claude skills/delegation parity are tracked in the build plan. Estimates for token/context/media size are not provider-exact unless a host supplies an exact counter.

Schemas above the safe inline-argv threshold use the documented system-prompt-file path plus strict agentkit local validation/correction; a live 40+ KB schema case passes. Schemas above the 256 KiB fallback bound fail closed. G10 attempt cost events Implemented Attempt start/finish events include usage and cost provenance. G14 workspace/native tools Implemented Per-call Claude permissions/tools/hooks and Codex sandbox/paths are verified by fake CLI argv tests; incompatible mode fields are refused. G15 MCP tool timeout Implemented CLI timeout derives from the tool timeout with a margin. G16 tool arguments/events Implemented API and native CLI tool events carry masked arguments, result digests/sizes, and optional host-masked previews bounded to 512 bytes. G17 images Implemented API, Codex and Claude Code image-result cases pass live checks; Claude Code MCP image serialization remains covered by the round-trip regression. The earlier failing report is retained as historical evidence. G18 long CLI sessions Partial Claude supports turn-bounded slices, resume/fork and stable-prefix flags; Codex supports fork. Codex exposes no verified turn-slice control, and stable-prefix behavior is Claude-specific. G19 first-event restart Implemented A first-event timeout can retry; idle timeout after output remains terminal. Identical-retry suppression stays host-owned. G20 CLI request hook Implemented Hook can replace validated argv while preserving the configured executable. G21 MCP skill source Implemented Pinned MCP skill resources are supported. G22 persona screening Implemented Optional host screening hook runs before composition. G23 native Claude subagents Partial Added fail-closed conversion from public AgentDefinition plus pinned persona resources to --agents; native skill installation and live delegated-agent conformance remain open. G24 scripted runtime fake Implemented Public scripted adapter/runtime factory is available with focused tests. G25 masked/bounded event sink Implemented MaskingSink applies host masking and bounded event values.

The earlier offline suite passed 5,958 tests with 98 skips. After the final regression additions, the full offline suite passes 5,961 tests with 98 skips. Ruff, strict typing and whitespace checks pass. A bounded live run on image_result and model_switch passed all seven model_switch rows, and passed image_result on Anthropic API, OpenAI API and Codex. Claude Code failed image_result before invoking its MCP tool; the retained report is tests/evals/reports/20261013T142237440683Z/summary.json. A focused Claude-only rerun after adding MCP image serialization failed the same way. Debugging showed spec.cli_kwargs() already supplied strict_mcp_config, while CliAdapter passed that argument a second time; the cognition constructor raised before spawning. The duplicate was removed, and a new offline regression covers one strict config flag. Live tool_evidence and image_result both pass on Claude Code alongside the other backends in tests/evals/reports/20261013T151551366051Z/summary.json.

The all-mode provider_auth_rejection eval uses a fresh deliberately invalid credential. Each backend returned an authentication failure in one attempt with zero observed usage and zero accounted spend; the report is tests/evals/reports/20261013T152207836480Z/summary.json. This validates real provider rejection shapes and confirms authentication failures do not retry. Transient 429/Retry-After still has offline parser/retry coverage only; no controlled provider 429 was induced. Claude Code's live long-schema fallback passed in tests/evals/reports/20261013T152051324301Z/summary.json.

The public additions are documented here as well as in the API reference: Credential, Workspace, ImagePart, ClaudePermissionMode, CodexSandboxMode, and McpSkillSource.

  • The two API modes are close. Retries, strict schemas with null cleaning, pricing, events and OTel exist and work.
  • The two CLI modes cannot carry Mirror today. Three gaps block them outright:
  • G1. A signed-in CLI login cannot be supplied. Credentials arrive only as env vars, and --bare disables Claude subscription OAuth.
  • G2. A login the CLI refreshes is deleted rather than handed back, so the stored copy dies.
  • G3. CLI failures are never classified and never retried.
  • Gaps that hold back the build and drive lanes but not preflight: native tools and per-call workspace (G14), tool arguments in events (G16), and long sessions (G18).

docs.title: G26. A Claude call without tools failed against the real CLI (fixed)
docs.text:
The no-tools default at models/providers/cli/calls.py:391 sends --mcp-config {}. Claude Code 2.1.296 rejects that: Error: Invalid MCP configuration: mcpServers: Invalid input: expected record, received undefined. It does so inline and as a file. {"mcpServers":{}} is accepted. This was checked against the real CLI with an invalid key, so nothing was spent. The no-tools default now uses the valid empty record, and FakeClaudeCli validates inline and file-backed config before consuming a scripted process result.

Prove: - the fake refuses {} and accepts {"mcpServers":{}}; - a no-tools call succeeds through the fake; - one opt-in real-CLI check with an invalid key reaches authentication rather than failing config parsing.

docs.title: G27. A budgeted CLI call does not retry a 429 that reported no cost (fixed)
docs.text:
R4 made each attempt get cap − spent. But a real CLI 429 carries no usage and no total_cost_usd, so spend is unknown, the guard at calls.py:639-648 fires, and the call ends limit_reached without retrying. This was reproduced with FakeClaudeCli: a 429 without usage under max_cost_usd=1 ends limit_reached.

Prove: a usage-less 429 under a cost cap is retried and answered. Its twin is an attempt with output but no cost, which still stops.

docs.title: G28. Non-string secrets reached events (fixed)
docs.text:
R3 masks string leaves only. A numeric or boolean secret, or one used as a dict key, reaches tool_call.arguments.

Prove: a numeric secret and a secret dict key never appear in a recorded event.

docs.title: G29. A host could not set TLS or proxy settings per adapter (fixed)
docs.text:
R2's allowlist (PATH, LANG, LC_*, TERM, NO_COLOR, TMP*) means SSL_CERT_FILE, NODE_EXTRA_CA_CERTS and proxy variables can arrive only ambiently, never through CliAdapter(env=). A deployment behind a corporate proxy or a private CA needs them per adapter.

CliTransportVariable provides a second named allowlist for TLS and proxy settings through transport=; those same names remain rejected through env=. Base URL and AWS credential variables are not transport settings and are rejected there too.

Prove: a transport setting passes through transport=; the same name passed as env= is refused; a *_BASE_URL is refused on every path.

Build: - one opt-in live check per CLI with a real login home. Claude: .credentials.json in CLAUDE_CONFIG_DIR. Codex: ChatGPT auth.json; - one with a refresh forced mid-call, asserting on_changed receives the new file.

On macOS, confirm whether Claude reads the file or the keychain, and fail closed if it reads the keychain.

Prove: both live checks pass and are recorded in tests/evals/reports/.

docs.title: G31. The argv bound could exceed the per-argument kernel limit (fixed)
docs.text:
max(4096, SC_ARG_MAX // 32) (models/providers/cli/_common.py:939-951) has no ceiling. On Linux with a large or unlimited stack it passes the 128 KiB per-argument limit (MAX_ARG_STRLEN), and an inline payload fails with E2BIG.

Prove: a payload just over the effective bound goes by file; just under goes inline; and the bound never exceeds the per-argument limit whatever SC_ARG_MAX reports.

docs.title: G32. The JSON extractor accepted the last object (reverted)
docs.text:
models/contracts/schema.py:100-106 used to refuse a reply holding more than one JSON object. It now takes the last. A reply that gives the answer and then an example object is read as the example.

The extractor again rejects more than one complete top-level object as ambiguous. A single stray closing brace remains tolerated. The regression test covers both behaviors.

docs.title: G33. UnpricedPolicy.REFUSE stopped refusing (reverted)
docs.text:
At core/runtime/calls.py:718-731, an unpriced token kind under REFUSE now degrades and answers with unknown cost whenever no cost cap is set. That makes REFUSE mean "proceed unpriced" in the common case.

REFUSE again fails the call when reported token categories cannot be priced. PROCEED_UNPRICED remains the explicit opt-in and preserves partial cost as mixed where possible.

docs.title: G34. Usage completeness was inferred from cost (fixed)
docs.text:
At core/runtime/calls.py:556, usage marked incomplete now counts as complete if the provider reports a cost. Cost and token counts are separate facts, and a ledger settling tokens needs to know when they are partial.

Answer.usage_complete is aggregated independently across turns. A reported cost can be present while token usage remains incomplete; a regression covers that combination.

docs.title: G35. A retried 429 makes the answer's cost unknown (P)
docs.text:
When a CLI attempt fails without reporting cost (a 429), the runtime sets the call's total_cost to unknown for good. The budget correctly treats that attempt as zero spent (G27). But the final Answer reports cost_usd=None, cost_source=unpriced, even when the attempt that succeeded reported its cost. Reproduced with FakeClaudeCli: a usage-less 429, then success at $0.20, gives an answer with an unknown cost.

A ledger reading the answer total then records every retried call as unpriced.

Build: an attempt that failed with no usage, no cost and no output contributes zero to the total, the same rule G27 applies to the budget. The total is unknown only when an attempt that produced output or usage reported no cost.

Prove: - a usage-less 429, then success at $0.20, gives cost_usd=0.20 with the source reported; - the twin is an attempt with output and no cost, which still leaves the total unknown.

docs.title: G43. One runtime: finish the migration to CallRuntime (architecture)
docs.text:
agentkit carries two runtimes side by side.

The current one is CallRuntime.ask/run, with AgentRunner.run_agent, Minds, compose, SkillSource, ToolSet, McpGateway, EventHub and WorkingContext/SessionHandle.

The older one is the Invoker, its middleware and RunContext.services, with: - Agent, RequestBuilder and Workflow; - agents/cognition, agents/policies, agents/control and agents/evaluation; - Observation/ObserverPort; - the state modules: compaction, memory, checkpoints, replay, stores, vectors and leases.

CallRuntime never touches the older runtime, and the two return different result and usage types with no conversion. The project's own docs name run_agent on CallRuntime as "one path for building a harness".

Why it matters: - Features read as available and are not. Compaction, memory, checkpoints, guardrails and observers exist and are tested, but no current caller reaches them. - Behaviour is duplicated. Retry, limits and pricing exist as middleware and again in CallRuntime; fixing one does not fix the other. - Downstream code breaks. Consumers built on the older path break when it is reorganised.

Build: one runtime. Each older piece is rebuilt on CallRuntime, or deleted.

Older piece Becomes Invoker, core/policies middleware, RunContext.services deleted; CallRuntime and the event sinks already do retry, limits, pricing, correction and tracing Observation, ObserverPort, integrations/observers deleted; EventHub subscribers state/compaction a context_policy: Callable[[WorkingContext], WorkingContext] that run/run_agent applies between slices and before resume; deterministic policies built in, summarising ones explicit opt-ins state/memory a memory provider run_agent turns into an untrusted context part at compose time state/checkpoints, state/replay, state/stores, state/vectors deleted; continuation is SessionHandle + FrozenContext with the core/serialization codecs; replay is the event journal state/leases (timed, renewed) deleted; admission is the untimed acquire hook agents/workflows.Workflow deleted; multi-step flows are the host's (or rebuilt over run_agent emitting CallEvents, if a real user appears) agents/cognition, agents/policies, agents/control, agents/evaluation, Agent, RequestBuilder, skills.Skill.as_agent, tools/adapters.as_tool deleted; Minds, run_agent, DelegationPolicy and the delegate tool cover them; grading is the host's integrations/mcp/approvals.ApprovalServer (bound to the old CLI class) rebuilt on the current CLI adapter's --permission-prompt-tool, with the same approval callback shape as McpPolicy.approval core/guardrails (check_url, redact, wrap_tool_output) kept as a library tools call, with an optional ToolSet hook

Order, so nothing breaks midway: 1. Rebuild the four pieces with current users: the compaction hook, the memory provider, approvals on the current CLI adapter, and G37–G42. 2. Delete the rest in one change, with docs and examples updated and no deprecation shims. Consumers still on the older path stay pinned to a pre-deletion revision until they move. 3. Add the claims test below.

Prove: - An architecture claims test in agentkit: one Answer type and one Usage type in the public surface; nothing imports a deleted module (a planted import of each is caught); every public module is reachable from CallRuntime or AgentRunner, or is a declared library (guardrails, serialization). - context_policy runs between slices, and the same transcript gives the same result. - A memory provider's items reach the composed prompt as an untrusted context part. - An approval prompt from the Claude CLI reaches the host callback on the current adapter.

Mirror's cognition already uses only the current runtime, so G43 changes no Mirror design. It moves compaction and memory hooks into agentkit, where Mirror plugs in its own policies.

Codex refuses it degrades: cost G50 an hours-long log that survives one bad write (working tree) the first exception from a sink turns it off for the rest of the call, and degraded is only reported at the end (calls.py:219-235,986-995) isolate each failure; emit degraded at once; keep delivering; stop only after N consecutive failures one failure mid-call: later events still arrive, and the degraded event is immediate degrades; follows G42 G51 Claude and Codex lanes in one process native_tool_policy is set once per runtime, and DENY refuses Codex (calls.py:410-416) native_tool_policy per call, never wider than the runtime's ceiling under one runtime, a Claude call denies native tools while a Codex call runs under warn blocks Codex starter lanes G52 a tool that ends the call to ask a person, resumable no suspended outcome (constants.py:40-46) ToolResult(stop_call=True) ends the call after the current turn, with a resumable session the tool ends a CLI call with the session id kept nice-to-have; A risk for G43: the current CLI adapter itself still uses Agent, RunContext and Budget internally (cli/calls.py:107,126,242-246,488-491). Deleting the older runtime has to move those internals into the adapter first, or G43 breaks every CLI call.

Forge does not need raw tool-call arguments from events. Its file, shell and grep tools are its own, so its wrappers see raw arguments, and its attestation comes from the workspace stamp and change journal. It needs the argument masker to be per-service policy, not agentkit's fixed default. agentkit already allows that, and should keep it.

Preflight on API keys G35, G36, the G34 cost-source rule, and the proving tests above Preflight on Claude or Codex logins All of the above, and G30: a recorded live run with a real .credentials.json and a ChatGPT auth.json, a refresh forced mid-call, and the macOS keychain question answered Forge build lanes G44, G45 and G51 (blocking); G46–G50 (degrading); G37 complete (stable_prefix, fork, native_agents through run_agent); G43 without breaking the CLI adapter's internals; the Codex limits in G5 and G18 accepted, which keeps build lanes on Claude Mirror run_agent (conversation, analysis loops) G37, G39, G42, and G43 step 1 (the compaction hook, the memory provider, approvals on the current CLI adapter)

docs.title: G1. A CLI login cannot be supplied (X)
docs.text:
Mirror today: - Logins are zipped session bundles holding Claude's credential files (M:packages/kernel/kernel/authority/session.py:230-275; the file set is in session_group.py:32-36). - Codex runs from either its bundle or codex login --with-api-key (M:assay/platform/providers/configured_agent.py:498-536).

agentkit: - CredentialRef.resolve() returns a Mapping[str, str] of env only (A:models/contracts/types.py:19-23). - The CLI adapter maps it to env (A:models/providers/cli/calls.py:163-182). - CliAdapter forces bare=True (cli/calls.py:204), and bare mode disables subscription OAuth (A:models/providers/cli/claude/driver.py:372-373,386). - IsolatedHome.restore() accepts only sessions/ and projects/*.jsonl (cli/isolation.py:113-122). - Codex gets a fresh home with no auth.json (isolation.py:77-80). Only the lower-level CodexCliCognition(config_home=…) can use one (codex/driver.py:401,1504-1505).

Build: - CredentialRef resolves to Credential(env: Mapping[str,str] = {}, home: Mapping[str, bytes] = {}). - home files are laid into the isolated home before spawn with mode 0600, from an allowlist per mode: - Claude: .credentials.json and the minimal settings it needs; - Codex: auth.json. - Anything outside the allowlist is refused before spawn, as an invalid request. - When home carries a Claude login, the adapter runs without --bare but keeps every isolation --bare bought: - --strict-mcp-config; - no user settings; - no hooks; - no auto-memory.

Make that an explicit option set rather than the single bare switch. - resolve becomes async. It is called inside async code today (cli/calls.py:163, frontiers/calls.py:48), and a host that releases from a vault over HTTP cannot block there.

Prove: per CLI, a fake that refuses to start unless the expected file is in its home at 0600. The twin is the env-only path, which still works. A file outside the allowlist is refused before spawn.

docs.title: G2. A refreshed login is never handed back (X)
docs.text:
Mirror today: seals the CLI home after the call and sends it back to the vault (finish, M:packages/kernel/kernel/authority/session_store.py:657-679). A borrower's refreshed token travels back to the group (session_group.py:179).

agentkit: deletes the credential files at close (A:models/providers/cli/isolation.py:24-27). snapshot() exports transcripts only (:83-101).

Build: - Credential carries on_changed: Callable[[Mapping[str, bytes]], Awaitable[None]] | None. - After the CLI exits, and before deletion, compare the allowlisted files with what was laid in. If any changed, await on_changed(changed) exactly once. - If the callback raises, the call's answer is kept, a degraded event records the failure, and the call still ends normally. - Deletion happens after the callback, on every exit path, cancellation included.

Prove: a fake CLI that rewrites its credential file triggers one callback with the new bytes. The twin is an unchanged file, which triggers none. A cancelled call still deletes the files after the callback.

docs.title: G3. CLI failures are unclassified and never retried (X)
docs.text:
Mirror today: retries api_error, rate_limit, overloaded and cli_reported_error on CLI calls (M:assay/platform/providers/model.py:216-225,1104-1119). It detects auth failures from CLI output (model.py:202-213), which is what makes the refresh-race retry possible (M:assay/platform/providers/execution.py:281-299,464-476).

agentkit: - CLI failures are always UNKNOWN or CANCELLED with retryable=False (A:models/providers/cli/calls.py:284-307). - The retry loop stops for any non-API mode (A:core/runtime/calls.py:481-483).

Build: - Classify the CLI's terminal event with the same classify used for APIs: - Claude: api_error_status, api_retry, result subtype; - Codex: turn.failed and error.code. - Map auth failures to FailureClass.AUTH. - Apply RetryPolicy to CLI modes. A retry is a new process in a fresh home with the credential resolved again, which is what makes the refresh-race case recover. - Emit retry with source="transport" and the class.

Prove: - a scripted 429 with retry-after, then success: one retry, after at least the advised wait; - the twin is a 400, which is never retried; - an auth failure is classified AUTH and retried only once, after resolve returns different credentials.

docs.title: G4. The executable and environment are fixed (X)
docs.text:
Mirror today: - passes its own claude binary (M:assay/platform/providers/model.py:1018); - sets MCP_TOOL_TIMEOUT, CLAUDE_CODE_DISABLE_AUTO_MEMORY and FORCE_PROMPT_CACHING_5M (M:forge/platform/providers/claude_cli.py:897-905, model.py:93).

agentkit: - CliAdapter(spawn, working_dir, native_tool_policy) only (A:models/providers/cli/calls.py:28-34); - the isolated env policy admits only the credential and passthrough variables (_common.py:501).

Build: - CliAdapter(executable: dict[Mode, str] | None, env: Mapping[str,str] | None); - env is merged after isolation and validated against a denylist, so credentials can only arrive through G1.

docs.title: Tier 1: blocks correct one-shot calls and correct money
G5. Mid-call cost and turn caps (X)
docs.text:
• Claude: --max-budget-usd is never sent. meter_spend=False (A:models/providers/cli/calls.py:185) makes _budget_cap return None (claude/driver.py:1281). The ceiling built at cli/calls.py:152-162 is unused, so max_cost_usd is only checked after the turn (A:core/runtime/calls.py:521-525). Mirror relies on the mid-call cap (M:forge/platform/providers/claude_cli.py:539-542). The installed Codex CLI 0.162.1 exposes no max-budget or max-turns option in codex exec --help; agentkit reports usage after the turn but cannot stop that process at an exact spend threshold.
  • Codex: has no budget flag (codex/driver.py:551-555). max_turns is passed to Claude only (cli/calls.py:206). The core's max_turns counts adapter turns (core/runtime/calls.py:349), and a CLI run is one.

Build: - Claude: send --max-budget-usd from CallLimits.max_cost_usd. - Codex: meter usage events as they stream, price them with the call's PriceTable, and stop the process group when the running cost crosses the cap. Count turns from turn events and stop at max_turns. - In both cases the outcome is limit_reached, with the partial usage settled.

Prove: scripted usage events that cross the cap mid-stream stop the process before the next event. The twin is a stream under the cap, which runs to completion.

docs.title: G6. Pricing policy is fixed to refusal (P)
docs.text:
Mirror today: - prices come from TOML (M:packages/kernel/kernel/authority/model_prices.toml); - cache rates are derived from the input rate (M:packages/kernel/kernel/authority/agent_adapter.py:544-546); - an unpriced model proceeds and is marked unpriced (:562-590).

agentkit: - PriceTable.load reads JSON (A:models/catalog/pricing.py:103-110); - every token kind needs an explicit rate (:131-134); - an unpriced model is refused before dispatch (A:core/runtime/calls.py:339-343); - an unpriced token kind fails after the money is spent (:516-520); - the bundled rows do not include the models Mirror runs.

Build: - UnpricedPolicy = REFUSE | PROCEED_UNPRICED, set per runtime. - PROCEED_UNPRICED dispatches, reports cost_source=unpriced, and is only allowed where the caller sets a turn or token cap. - An unpriced token kind after dispatch fails under REFUSE. Under PROCEED_UNPRICED, the answer is preserved and any priced portion reports cost_source=mixed. - PriceTable.derive(input=…, output=…, cache_read_ratio=…, cache_write_ratio=…) covers providers that publish ratios. - PriceTable.load accepts TOML as well as JSON.

Prove: an unpriced model is refused under REFUSE, dispatched under PROCEED_UNPRICED; a missing token rate fails under REFUSE and yields mixed under PROCEED_UNPRICED.

docs.title: G7. No real bound on concurrent CLI processes (X)
docs.text:
Mirror today: bounds spawns by a measured admission ceiling (M:assay/platform/providers/model.py:1029).

agentkit: the semaphore is keyed on config_dir (A:models/providers/cli/_common.py:77-90), and config_dir is unique per call (cli/calls.py:203), so the semaphore never binds.

Build: - one semaphore per (runtime, mode), sized by a CallRuntime(max_concurrent_cli=…) the host passes; - an acquire hook so a host can supply its own admission (Mirror's measured memory and CPU window).

docs.title: G8. Answer decoding and repair are too narrow (P)
docs.text:
Mirror today: - accepts a fenced block, a stray trailing brace, and the last JSON object in the last message (M:forge/platform/providers/claude_cli.py:2823-2876, M:control/tenancy/adapters/system/providers/chat_agent.py:851-855); - configures the number of repairs, and adds validators that check evidence references (M:assay/platform/providers/model.py:910-918).

agentkit: json.loads(text) as the fallback (A:core/runtime/calls.py:605), and exactly one schema-only correction (:612).

Build: - A tolerant extractor, applied only to the last message: - strip one fence; - take the last balanced top-level object; - drop one trailing unmatched brace. - OutputSpec(max_corrections=1, validators=[Callable[[value], list[str]]]). Validator errors are fed back into the correction turn exactly like schema errors.

Prove: each tolerated form decodes. The twin is two objects in the last message with no clear last one, which fails as invalid rather than guessing. A validator error triggers a correction turn.

docs.title: G9. A long schema goes on argv (X)
docs.text:
The installed Claude Code 2.1.296 help and current CLI reference expose --json-schema <schema> as inline JSON but no file-backed schema option. The adapter therefore does not invent a --json-schema-file flag. For schemas above 32 KiB and up to 256 KiB, it uses the documented --append-system-prompt-file mechanism to provide schema guidance, then the core parser, validator and correction turn enforce the actual contract. This is an explicit degradation from provider-native constrained output, surfaced as a structured_output degradation event. The larger-schema live case validates this path. See Anthropic's CLI reference and structured output guide.

Mirror today: keeps the schema off argv when it is too long (M:packages/kernel/kernel/authority/schema_fit.py).

agentkit: --json-schema goes straight onto argv (A:models/providers/cli/claude/driver.py:1423).

Build: pass the schema through a file in the isolated home when its encoded size crosses the platform's argv room. Measure that from os.sysconf('SC_ARG_MAX'); never hardcode it.

docs.title: G10. No per-attempt cost event (P)
docs.text:
Mirror today: announces and settles spend per attempt (M:forge/platform/providers/claude_cli.py:404-462,722; control's claude_agent.py:631).

agentkit: call_started and call_finished exist and are awaited (A:core/runtime/calls.py:210-220,696-703). A retried call reports one total.

Build: attempt_started(attempt, mode, model) and attempt_finished(attempt, outcome, usage, cost_usd, cost_source) events between them, so a ledger can settle every attempt that spent money.

docs.title: Tier 2: blocks the build and drive lanes (not preflight)
G11. Shared login across concurrent calls (X)
docs.text:
Mirror today: many concurrent calls share one vault lease by borrowing snapshots of one CLI home (M:packages/kernel/kernel/authority/session_store.py:391-445, session_group.py:88-249).

Decision before building: it may belong in the host rather than in agentkit. With G1 and G2, a host can serialise per login, or hand out snapshots and merge refreshed tokens itself. Recommended: keep it in the host, and have agentkit only guarantee that G2's callback fires once per call with the final files.

docs.title: G12. Read-only credential mode (X)
docs.text:
Mirror today: chat uses a snapshot that may refresh locally but never writes back (M:packages/kernel/kernel/authority/session_store.py:369-389).

Build: this falls out of G2: on_changed=None means discard.

docs.title: G13. Home cleanup and placement (P)
docs.text:
• Cleanup is registered with atexit only (A:models/providers/cli/isolation.py:75). A SIGTERM from a container stop leaves credential files on disk until the next sweep.
  • Build: delete credential files from a SIGTERM/SIGINT handler that chains to any existing one, which is what Mirror's session.py:107-124 does.
  • IsolatedHome(parent=) exists (isolation.py:62), but CliAdapter constructs it without a parent (cli/calls.py:117).
  • Build: CliAdapter(home_parent=Path).

docs.title: G14. Native tools, workspace and permissions are fixed (X)
docs.text:
Mirror today: - build lanes run Claude Code with Read, Edit and Bash behind a PreToolUse fence, with read receipts (M:assay/platform/providers/model.py:1007-1030, evidence_reads.py, M:forge/platform/providers/claude_cli.py:884-917); - the working directory, extra dirs, settings and permission mode are set per call (claude_cli.py:1283,1394-1402).

agentkit: - Claude: no native tools, bare (A:models/providers/cli/calls.py:198-209); - Codex: read-only sandbox, shell off (:212-236); - the working directory is fixed per adapter (:37,171).

Build: a per-call Workspace(working_dir, add_dirs, permission_mode, native_tools: set[str], hooks: HookSpec | None, sandbox: CodexSandbox | None) on run(). The hook spec is passed through as a generated settings file, so a host fence (Mirror's agent_hooks) runs as the CLI's own PreToolUse hook. Native tool use is reported in events (G16).

docs.title: G15. The CLI's MCP tool timeout is not derived (P)
docs.text: codex_kwargs() is called without a timeout, and Claude's MCP_TOOL_TIMEOUT is never set (A:models/providers/cli/calls.py:226-230). Both should come from ToolSet.timeout_s (A:tools/execution/policy.py:90) plus a margin, so the CLI never times out a tool the server is still allowed to run.

docs.title: G16. Tool-call arguments are missing from events (X)
docs.text:
Mirror today: records each tool call's arguments in build events, with file bodies recorded as shape only (M:forge/…/stream_events.py:295-351). It reports what Codex read as evidence (shell_read_paths, M:assay/platform/providers/configured_agent.py:407-428).

agentkit: - API mode carries argument_digest only (A:core/runtime/calls.py:538-543); - CLI mode carries the tool name only (cli/calls.py:250-251); - full arguments end up only in Answer.context (:100-114).

Build: - tool_call events carry arguments passed through a host ArgumentMasker(tool, args) -> args (the default replaces string values over a size with {len, sha256}); - tool_result carries size, overflowed and an optional masked preview; - the same events come from native CLI tools under G14.

docs.title: G17. Images in the prompt (X)
docs.text:
Mirror today: passes images to Codex (M:assay/platform/providers/configured_agent.py:349-352).

agentkit: ComposedPrompt has no image parts (A:agents/prompts/composition.py:36-40).

Build: image parts in ComposedPrompt, mapped per mode. A mode that cannot take them emits degraded and refuses rather than silently dropping them.

docs.title: G18. Long sessions on the CLI (P)
docs.text:
Mirror today: continues, resumes and forks Claude sessions across slices (M:forge/platform/providers/claude_cli.py:1187-1188,1489-1491,1575), and keeps a stable cached prefix (stable_prompt_prefix=True, M:assay/platform/providers/model.py:1023).

agentkit: - turns_per_slice works only in the API tool loop (A:core/runtime/calls.py:599); - CLI resume uses cli_session_id and a transcript bundle capped at 16 MiB (cli/calls.py:118-146,184, isolation.py:83); - there is no fork, and no stable-prefix option.

Build: - turns_per_slice on CLI modes: stop the process at the slice's turn count and return a SessionHandle; - fork=True on resume; - stable_prefix=True passed to the CLI.

Prove: a three-slice run on each CLI fake resumes with the same session id and a growing transcript.

docs.title: G19. Stall restart is terminal (X)
docs.text:
Mirror today: restarts a starved call within the admission window (M:assay/platform/providers/execution.py:306-362,199-210).

agentkit: an idle_s or first_event_s breach ends as limit_reached and is never retried (A:core/runtime/calls.py:310-313,472-474).

Build: classify a first_event_s breach (nothing at all arrived) as TIMEOUT, which is retryable, and an idle_s breach after output as terminal. Only the first is safe to repeat. Mirror's "refuse an identical retry after a timeout" (execution.py:479-490) stays in the host.

docs.text: # Gap Evidence Build G20 request_hook exists only for API modes A:models/providers/frontiers/calls.py:27 A CLI equivalent, a hook over the built argv and settings. (result_hook on MCP serving does exist: A:integrations/mcp/serve.py:294,532,753.) G21 Skills: no MCP skill:// source A:agents/skills/resources.py:87-160 An MCP resource source G22 User-authored persona text is moved, not screened A:agents/prompts/composition.py:61 A screening hook (no secrets, no verdict claims) before composition G23 Native Claude Code skills and subagents are unused --agents exists (claude/driver.py:375,1403) but bare mode passes none Map definitions onto --agents when G1's non-bare option set is used; a conformance scenario per mode G24 No public scripted fake for CallRuntime only tests/source/conformance/test_calls.py:54 Ship agentkit.testing.ScriptedAdapter and scripted_runtime(turns, pricing) G25 Journals are not masked or bounded generically events carry digests (core/runtime/calls.py:206-207); the CLI diagnostic is redacted and cut (cli/calls.py:290-306) A MaskingSink(inner, masker, max_field_bytes) wrapper for any EventSink

docs.title: Stays in Mirror, not agentkit
docs.text: These are host policy. Mirror keeps them on top of the call contract: - admission control by measured memory and CPU (M:assay/platform/providers/admission.py), plugged in through G7's hook; - prompt fitting and splitting (fitting.py, packages/prompting/fit); - the login refresh holder and borrowers (one refresh holder per CLI login, any number of borrowers) and compare-and-set rotation in the vault — no timed leases (on top of G1, G2 and G12); - the stage-tier to model mapping (agentkit's ModelSettings.tier is a presentation hint, models/contracts/settings.py:16,43-46); - refusing an identical retry after a timeout; - the ledger.

docs.title: Breakage when Mirror moves its pin
docs.text:
Mirror tracks branch = "main" (M:pyproject.toml:158, M:packages/agent_skills/pyproject.toml:26), so any lock refresh pulls f8d20c1 in and breaks every plane at import.

Modules that no longer exist: agentkit.runtime, .testing, .capabilities, .adapters, .kernel, .middlewares, .memory, .prompts, .integrations.claude_cli and .agents.cognition.claude_cli.

Other moves: - the package root exports only six namespaces (A:__init__.py:3-6); - ClaudeCliCognition and CodexCliCognition moved to A:models/providers/cli/__init__.py:12-34.

Non-test import sites:

Area Files assay platform/providers/{agentkit_sdk,configured_agent,evidence_fence,model}.py control tenancy/adapters/system/providers/{agentkit_api,chat_agent,chat_memory,chat_registry,claude_agent,codex_agent}.py evals adapters/{agentkit_model,codex_cli,local_model,runtimes}.py forge platform/providers/{agent_tools_adapter,agentkit_sdk,attestation,checkpoints,claude_cli,compaction,event_stream,mcp_server,policy,starter,tool_lifecycle,tool_registry}.py packages agent_hooks/…/claude_cli_fence.py, agent_skills/…/integrations/agentkit.py, cognition/…/vendor/agentkit.py sounding platform/guardrail.py

About 40 test files are affected as well.

Mirror's EngineServer and EvidenceServer subclass private seams of McpServerSpec (_dispatch, _write_config, _document, _asgi_app; still present at A:integrations/mcp/serve.py:301,445,647,709). They work, but any refactor there breaks them silently.

Do now, before anything else: pin Mirror to rev = "555bc57…" instead of branch = "main". Move the pin deliberately, plane by plane, once the gaps a plane needs are closed.

docs.title: Order
docs.text:
1. G1, G2, G3, G4. Without these no CLI mode carries a real login.
  2. G5, G6, G8, G10. The money must be right and a correct answer must not be thrown away.
  3. G7, G9, G13, G24. Small and contained.

That is everything preflight needs, which makes it the first consumer.

Next, for assay's drive and forge's build lanes: 4. G14, G16, G15, G18, G19, G17.

Then: 5. G20–G23, G25, the design items.

Each gap ships with its conformance scenario run across all four modes, or explicitly marked not-applicable for a mode with the reason, in tests/source/conformance/.
